en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on the Maiden (Kumāribhūtavagga) 79.
The Training Rule on the Abode of Sorrow (Sokāvāsasikkhāpada).
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the nun Thullanandā gave the full admission to the trainee Caṇḍakāḷī, who was associated with men, associated with boys, fierce, and a dwelling place for grief.
Those nuns who were modest... [as before] ...were indignant, complained, and grumbled:
"How can the noble lady Thullanandā give the full admission to the trainee Caṇḍakāḷī, who is associated with men, associated with boys, fierce, and a dwelling place for grief?"... [as before] ...
“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā ordains a trainee nun named Caṇḍakāḷī—one who is associated with men, associated with boys, fierce, and a dwelling place of grief?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her … [as before] …
“How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā give the full admission to the trainee Caṇḍakāḷī, who is associated with men, associated with boys, fierce, and a dwelling place of grief?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of those with faith...
And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:”
“Whatever nun, however, should give the full admission to a trainee nun who is associated with men, associated with boys, fierce, and a dwelling place of grief, it is an offense entailing expiation.
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun... [and so on].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"A man" means:
One who has reached twenty years of age.
A "boy" (kumāraka) is one who has not reached twenty years of age.
"Intimately associated" means intimately associated with improper bodily and verbal conduct.
"Fierce" means...
One who is prone to anger is so called.
One who dwells in sorrow is said to produce suffering for others and to be possessed by sorrow.
A *sikkhamānā* is one who has trained in the six rules for two years.
"Should ordain" means:
If she should ordain [a woman], or if,
intending "I will give the full admission," she seeks a group, a preceptor, a bowl, or a robe, or demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
With the formal motion (ñatti), there is an offense of wrong-doing.
For two formal proclamations (*kammavācā*), there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
At the conclusion of the formal proclamation, the preceptor (*upajjhāyā*) incurs an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*);
for the community (*gaṇa*) and the teacher (*ācariyā*), there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if she ordains her without knowing [the facts],
or if she is insane.
"By one who is a first offender.
The ninth training rule is concluded.
